name: osteoarthritis overview
title: Osteoarthritis as a chronic monoarthritis: rule out red flags, make the clinical diagnosis, stage it on X-ray, then treat with biomechanical and education measures at every stage, medicines for symptoms, and joint replacement only for end-stage disease; arthroscopy is not recommended

root.title: ONE joint aching for over 6 weeks, worse with activity: osteoarthritis (OA) until a red flag says otherwise
lines: OA is a CLINICAL diagnosis: typical symptoms + NO other cause · the X-ray STAGES it, it does not diagnose it
first set aside mechanical and sports causes of knee pain (no arthritis)

groups.title: IS IT OA?
lines: knee >> hip; ankle; shoulder >> big toe

groups.title: TREAT IT: what stage, what can be fixed?
lines: no treatment preserves the joint; all improve life WITH it

head: h
Red flag → NOT OA
think something else
clue: • warm or hot joint: infection, crystals
tx: MRI or bone scan only when the diagnosis is in DOUBT

head: h
Osteoarthritis
a 'sick joint': every tissue fails to heal
clue: • female 1.4× · post-traumatic OA (after an anterior cruciate ligament tear) starts young

head: h
Every stage: biomechanics + education
alignment · overuse · weakness · gait
clue: • neuromuscular exercise physiotherapy, ≥ 3 months (Tai-Chi, GLA:D program)

head: h
Medicines: symptoms only
less pain, better function
clue: • oral NSAID if no contraindication (not in kidney failure)
• refractory: steroid injection (short-term), then a duloxetine trial 2–3 months
tx: • injected hyaluronic acid, platelet-rich plasma, stem cells
• opioids: generally avoid (tramadol at most; others: risks > benefit)

head: h
Surgery: END STAGE only
unacceptable symptoms despite all of the rest
clue: a salvage procedure · strong evidence of benefit
• X-ray bone on bone → refer to orthopedics
tx: ± meniscectomy or repair: no meaningful benefit
